title: Family Cycling Days Out: Traffic-Free Trails and Tips
description: Family cycling days out: traffic-free trails on old railway lines and forest tracks, bike hire, kids’ bike safety, trailers and planning a route.
intro: Flat, car-free trails, a café halfway and the wind in your hair. Cycling is a cheap, healthy family day out that teens enjoy too.

image.alt: A family walking through a field with their dog

cardText: Traffic-free trails, bike hire and safety tips.

blocks.title: Scout’s cycling tip
blocks.text: Pick a route about half as long as you think. You can always do more, but tired legs miles from the car are no fun.
points: Check tyres and brakes before you go
Old railway paths are flat and gentle

sections.html: Former railway lines, canal towpaths (check local rules), forest trails and country parks often have traffic-free routes. Many forests have colour-graded trails and bike hire. In the US, rail trails and state parks offer the same.

• Balance bikes for toddlers.
  • Child seats, trailers or tag-alongs for younger kids.
  • Helmets, bright clothes, water and snacks.
Choose a route with a playground or café halfway. Find more in karts, skates and bikes and nature days out.

faqs.a: Traffic-free routes such as old railway lines, forest trails and country park paths are the safest places for families to ride.
